messages:
alex kim: Quick sync — model-ingress ownership question. I want to propose we split responsibility: infra owns the fast perf-smoke (latency, memory, basic int8 path checks), ML owns deep quality bench and golden artifacts. Duplicating fullbench across teams is costing weeks for intake.

maya singh: +1 to separation in responsibility. ML keeps golden prompts/refs and quality thresholds. We need a clear manifest contract for metadata (tokenizer, seqlen, seed, eval-set) so infra can run deterministic checks.

sergey petrov: Concern: if infra only runs tiny smoke we miss regressions that only show up in quantized variants at scale. Suggest an "ensemble-smoke" that includes the most-likely runtime variants (fp16, int8) but at a sampled scale.

nina r.: Agree with manifest. Also we need to fix artifact storage/permissions — bench-bucket currently has ad-hoc ACLs causing onboarding delays. A signed manifest in the model registry would help with access checks.

maya singh: Example manifest snippet:
```json
{"model_id":"m-2026-0422","tokenizer":"sentencepiece_v2","seqlen":2048,"artifact_sha":"abc123def","eval_set":"gold_v2","repro_seed":42}
```

infra-bot: Deploy-check: artifact-manifest v1 published to registry (sha:abc123def). link: https://reg.internal/models/manifest/abc123def

alex kim: Nice, manifest is useful. Another thing: runtime should expose a light "compat-score" header from the ingress that summarizes tokenization/kv/perf checks so automated gates can act without downloading artifacts.

jordan: Compat-score sounds promising but needs a strict definition. Proposal: float 0..1, aggregated from three components: tokenization_match, kv_compat (binary), perf_safety (0..1). Keep it intentionally coarse to avoid churn.

maya singh: Tokenization and kv checks are cheap. Perf_safety needs a small microbench on representative inputs — infra can run that in a sandbox on incoming model versions.

sergey petrov: Tradeoff: fullbench vs sampled bench. Fullbench stalls intake. Staged acceptance is better: 1) smoke (fast), 2) sampled bench (1000 golden prompts), 3) fullbench on dedicated pool before GA. This also mirrors Dedicated flows for customers that need guaranteed throughput.

nina r.: Staged acceptance + canary traffic is the right operational posture. Add a mandatory fallback: if new model breaks production, auto-rollback to previous variant and page SRE.

ops-liz: Rollback exists in rollout-service but we need the wiring: model registry version ids -> rollout-service -> observability circuit-breaker. I'll own wiring once we define the compat signals.

alex kim: Action items (tentative): 1) maya + nina: draft manifest schema including ACL/KMS fields (deadline Thu). 2) sergey + infra: prototype ensemble-smoke that runs fp16 + int8 shadow on 1k inputs (deadline next Tue). 3) jordan + ops: wire rollback hooks and compat-score into rollout-service (deadline EOW).

jordan: I'll create tickets on the rollout board and tag @oncall for the integration window.

maya singh: One more governance point: ML sets quality thresholds (e.g., perplexity delta, top-k exact match) but infra gates on runtime signals. We should publish the threshold list in the manifest so automation can apply it.

sergey petrov: Reproducibility note: require deterministic seeds + tokenizer version in manifest. I'll add a `repro_seed` and `tokenizer_hash` fields to ensure evals can be rerun.

nina r.: Also include an access-control section for private/corp models (KMS key id, allowed orgs). Can't assume all artifacts are public.

infra-bot: Reminder: sync meeting Fri 10:00 to review prototype. Attendees: alex kim, maya singh, sergey petrov, nina r., jordan, ops-liz.

jordan: Will prepare rollout diagrams and a short sequence diagram for the compat-score flow. :thumbsup:

maya singh: I'll draft the manifest proto and open a short PR in #eng-ml-docs for review.

sergey petrov: Prototype plan detail: run int8 shadow inference on 1k golden prompts, compute token-level edit distance + latency distribution. Keep initial run cheap so we iterate quickly.

ops-liz: We'll add a canary playbook to ops-runbooks and wire alerts to the circuit-breaker signal.

alex kim: Sounds like a plan. I'll start a short RFC tomorrow to formalize the acceptance contract and ownership split. If anyone objects to the responsibilities split, flag it here; otherwise we'll proceed.

nina r.: No objections from me. Please ensure PII handling and ACLs are explicit in the RFC.

alex kim: Will include KMS/ACL section. End of thread.
